intro: Our wet-lab work is organized into Platform and Function. The scaffold-group contribution to Platform covers the construction and production of protein scaffolds, hydrogel preparation and characterization, cellular evaluation, and the ligation system. Within each experiment, the corresponding results and supporting figures are presented alongside the experimental description. Function is organized into magnetically responsive anisotropy, GAG retention and delivery.
platformHtml:
1 Hydrogel scaffold

We first verified the normal expression and purification of the scaffold protein and used the purified protein to prepare hydrogel precursor solutions to validate the photocrosslinking method, and then determined the mechanical properties and biocompatibility of the material. On this basis, we expanded the scaffold from a single length to a series in which both length and interface density are programmable, and verified that the same expression and purification procedure is applicable to all constructs in the series.

1.1 Design of the scaffold plasmid: a PRe-RDL platform enabling recursive doubling and interface insertion

Scaffold plasmid design

Experiment

The 2KY scaffold consists of tandem repeats of a 171-bp (57-aa) unit, (GAGAGS)₂–GRGDS–GKGVP–(GVGVP)₃–GYGVP–(GVGVP)₃. It belongs to the family of silk–elastin-like proteins (SELPs), which combine silk-like (GAGAGS) and elastin-like (GVGVP) sequences,([1]) and additionally encodes tyrosine, lysine and RGD motifs.([2])

Highly repetitive genes of this type cannot be extended by conventional PCR or homologous recombination: every repeat constitutes an identical primer-binding site, so that a primer annealing within the repeat region initiates extension from all repeats simultaneously, generating products that differ from one another by one repeat unit in length and cannot be separated at the scale of the whole plasmid.

To overcome this limitation, instead of treating 2KY-5 as a fixed sequence, we designed it as a cassette that can be doubled recursively, following the plasmid reconstruction recursive directional ligation (PRe-RDL) strategy developed by the Chilkoti group.([3])

Specifically, a BseRI recognition site (GAGGAG) was embedded in the GGGGS linker 14 bp upstream of the repeat array, and an AcuI recognition site (CTTCAG on the coding strand) was embedded in the GGSGGSSGS trailer 17 bp downstream. Both are type IIS restriction enzymes that cleave outside their recognition sequences: BseRI cuts 10/8 nt and AcuI 16/14 nt away from the recognition site, each leaving a 2-nt 3′ overhang. The phases of the two flanking linkers were designed such that both overhangs are GG, identical to the first two bases of the repeat array.

Consequently, the plasmid is digested with AcuI + XbaI and with BseRI + XbaI in parallel, the gene-containing half of each digest is recovered, and the two pieces are ligated; in a single cycle, this doubles the repeat array and reconstitutes the plasmid, with no extra bases remaining at the junction and the reading frame unchanged. Both enzyme sites remain outside the doubled array, so the cycle can be repeated indefinitely.

A key feature of this design is that the enzyme recognition sites lie within the flanking linkers and never within the repeat sequence itself. The approach is therefore not constrained by the codon degeneracy of glycine/alanine-rich sequences such as 2KY, which is precisely the obstacle that classical RDL cannot overcome for such sequences.

In addition, we reserved three docking sites for SnoopTag2 on the plasmid. Their positions relative to the two cut sites determine the fate of the tag during doubling (Table 1.1.1):

Table 1.1.1. Positions of the three SnoopTag2 docking sites relative to the cut sites, their behavior during a doubling round, and the resulting constructs.

Tag insertion sitePosition relative to cut siteBehavior during a doubling roundResulting construct
N-terminus (before NdeI)Upstream of the BseRI cut siteNot duplicated; remains a single copyTag–[2KY-5]n
End of the gene (before the trailer)Upstream of the AcuI cut siteDuplicated together with the repeat unit[2KY-5-Tag]n
C-terminus (before the stop codon)Downstream of the AcuI cut siteNot duplicated; remains a single copy[2KY-5]n–Tag

In this project, we adopted the second site, such that each 2KY-5 block is followed by one SnoopTag2. Scaffold length and interface number thereby become a jointly programmable quantity, rather than two variables that must be constructed separately.

Results

Accordingly, we obtained a single parental plasmid, pET19b-2KY5-RDL (6636 bp; Figure 1.1.1), by whole-gene synthesis; all other three constructs were derived from it experimentally.

1.2 Scaffold protein 2KY-5

1.2.1 Expression of the scaffold protein 2KY-5
Transformation and sequence verification

Experiment

The synthesized pET19b-2KY5-RDL was transformed into E. coli BL21(DE3) for protein expression, and colonies of successful transformants were obtained (Figure 1.2.1.1). Plasmid identity was first verified by colony PCR. Because the insert consists of perfectly repeated sequences, we used the T7 promoter and T7 terminator primers, which anneal outside the insert, as the forward and reverse primers. This primer pair is common to all constructs in this series, and the product size varies with the repeat number, so that the copy number can be read directly from the band position.

Results

Agarose gel electrophoresis of the PCR products showed a band at 1152 bp, consistent with the theoretical size of 2KY-5 (Figure 1.2.1.2), and sequencing of the insert from the submitted cultures confirmed that its sequence was correct.

Expression and soluble recovery

Experiment

The expression strain was then inoculated into LB medium containing Amp and cultured to mid-logarithmic phase, after which expression was induced with 1 mM IPTG (final concentration) for approximately 6 h. Cells were harvested and lysed by sonication, and the supernatant was collected. Samples of the culture before and after induction, the lysate supernatant and the lysate pellet were analyzed by SDS-PAGE (Figure 1.2.1.3).

Results

No band was present at the expected molecular weight before induction, whereas a band appeared after induction, demonstrating successful IPTG induction without leaky expression. In addition, the target band was present in the lysate supernatant but faint in the pellet, indicating that cell lysis is a feasible method for the initial recovery of 2KY-5.

1.2.2 Purification of the scaffold protein 2KY-5
Optimization of inverse transition cycling

Experiment

We purified 2KY-5 from the cell lysate supernatant by inverse transition cycling (ITC).([4]) In preliminary experiments, we found that the original conditions caused considerable protein loss during the high-temperature phase-transition step. To improve the purification yield, we performed a gradient screen of two parameters in this step, the NaCl concentration of the buffer and the heating temperature.

SDS-PAGE was performed on the supernatant after heating (H-Sup.) and the supernatant after cooling (C-Sup.) under each condition, and the condition with the highest recovery was identified preliminarily by comparing the band intensities of the two samples. An intense H-Sup. band indicates a large amount of protein that was not recovered during purification, whereas an intense C-Sup. band indicates a high protein yield after purification.

Results

The results showed that raising the temperature had little effect on the purification yield, whereas the NaCl concentration of the buffer was the more influential factor, and that the buffer containing 2 M NaCl gave the highest yield (Figure 1.2.2.1 and Figure 1.2.2.2). This trend is consistent with the reported regulation of the phase-transition temperature of elastin-like polypeptides by salt ions.([5])

Purification under the selected conditions

Experiment

Subsequent purifications were carried out under the optimal conditions identified (heating to 65 °C; PBS containing 2 M NaCl). Samples of the lysate supernatant, the supernatant after the high-temperature phase transition, the pellet obtained after cooling-induced redissolution, and the supernatant after cooling were collected during ITC and analyzed by SDS-PAGE to confirm the purification effect.

Results

Compared with the initial lysate supernatant, the contaminating protein bands were absent from the cooled supernatant collected after ITC, and the band corresponding to 2KY-5 was present only in the final solution, with almost no loss during the process, indicating excellent purification (Figure 1.2.2.3).

Concentration of the purified protein

Experiment

The purified 2KY-5 supernatant was concentrated using ultrafiltration tubes with a 10-kDa molecular weight cut-off (3,500 × g, 30 min), yielding approximately 5 mL of concentrated solution.

Results

The protein concentrations before and after concentration were determined by the BCA assay,([6]) giving a concentration factor of approximately 3.5, with essentially no protein loss (Figure 1.2.2.4).

Dialysis, lyophilization and yield

Experiment

The solution was then dialyzed for 24 h to remove residual salt, and the dialyzed solution was stored at −80 °C. Once completely frozen, a layer of filter paper was wrapped over the top of the tube, and the sample was rapidly transferred to a freeze dryer and lyophilized for 12 h to obtain a lyophilized powder, which was stored for subsequent hydrogel preparation. The detailed workflow and equipment in our laboratory are shown in Figure 1.2.2.5.

Results

Based on the calculated yield, approximately 500 mg of protein was obtained per liter of bacterial culture. This is a high yield under the routine protein-induction conditions currently used in our laboratory, making the process suitable for further optimization of the production conditions toward industrial-scale mass production, and giving it high commercial value.

1.2.3 Photocrosslinking of 2KY-5 and preparation of the hydrogel
Blue-light photocrosslinking

Experiment

Using the prepared 2KY-5 lyophilized powder, we prepared a 10% (w/v) hydrogel precursor solution containing 2 mM ruthenium (Ru) and 20 mM sodium persulfate (SPS) as the photocrosslinker and placed it in a 1.5-mL microcentrifuge tube. Under visible light, the Ru/SPS system catalyzes the formation of covalent dityrosine crosslinks between adjacent tyrosine residues([7,8]) (Figure 1.2.3.1). The system was then irradiated with 450-nm blue light, and after 2 s of irradiation the tube was inverted to observe the state of its contents.

View the combined photocrosslinking figure

Results

The non-irradiated solution flowed to the bottom of the tube upon inversion, whereas the irradiated sample remained in place, demonstrating that the system was fully crosslinked after 2 s of blue-light irradiation (Figure 1.2.3.2; Supplementary Movies S1 and S2).

Figure 1.2.3.2. Appearance before and after photocrosslinking. Left, hydrogel precursor solution before illumination; right, hydrogel formed after 2 s of 450-nm blue-light irradiation.

1.2.4 Characterization of the hydrogel
Hydrogel morphology

Experiment

Scanning electron microscopy (SEM).

Results

Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) showed that the hydrogel has an interconnected, three-dimensional porous network with pores of varying size (Figure 1.2.4.1). Such a porous architecture may facilitate the diffusion of nutrients and metabolites.

Fluorescence characterization

Experiment

To verify the chemical nature of the crosslinking, three-dimensional excitation–emission matrix (EEM) fluorescence spectra of the precursor solution and the resulting hydrogel were recorded (Figure 1.2.4.2).

Results

The precursor solution showed a fluorescence peak at an excitation wavelength of approximately 280 nm and an emission wavelength of approximately 300–310 nm, corresponding to the intrinsic fluorescence of tyrosine. After gelation, the main fluorescence peak shifted to an excitation wavelength of approximately 330 nm and an emission wavelength of approximately 400 nm, with markedly increased intensity. Emission near 400 nm is characteristic of dityrosine,([9]) suggesting that dityrosine crosslinks formed between tyrosine residues upon illumination.

Viscoelastic properties

Experiment

Frequency-sweep rheology over 0.1–100 rad/s.

Results

Frequency-sweep rheology (Figure 1.2.4.3) showed that, over the entire range of 0.1–100 rad/s, the storage modulus (G′) of all three hydrogels (2Y-5, 2KY-5 and 2KY-16) exceeded the loss modulus (G″) by at least approximately two orders of magnitude and was essentially independent of frequency, indicating that photocrosslinking produced a stable, predominantly elastic, solid-like network.

The G′ values of 2Y-5 and 2KY-5 were similar (approximately 2–3 kPa), whereas that of 2KY-16 reached approximately 20 kPa, nearly one order of magnitude higher. We speculate that this may be related to the larger number of crosslinking sites provided by the longer scaffold chains and the resulting reduction in dangling chain ends (a hypothesis that remains to be tested experimentally).

Stress–strain behavior

Experiment

Stress–strain testing and calculation of Young’s moduli.

Results

The stress–strain curves (Figure 1.2.4.4A) showed that, within a strain range of 0–0.3, the stress of all three hydrogels increased nonlinearly with strain; the stress of 2KY-16 (approximately 23 kPa at a strain of 0.3) was clearly higher than that of 2Y-5 and 2KY-5 (approximately 15 kPa), whose curves nearly overlapped. The Young’s moduli calculated accordingly were approximately 29 kPa for 2Y-5, 30 kPa for 2KY-5 and 53 kPa for 2KY-16; there was no significant difference between 2Y-5 and 2KY-5 (ns), whereas 2KY-16 was significantly higher than both (p < 0.001) (Figure 1.2.4.4B). Thus, increasing the repeat number from 5 to 16 effectively enhanced the mechanical strength of the hydrogel.

Figure 1.2.4.4. Stress–strain curves and Young’s moduli of the hydrogels. (A) Stress–strain curves over a strain range of 0–0.3. (B) Young’s moduli. ns, not significant; ***, p < 0.001.

Adhesion and qualitative demonstrations

Experiment

Shear adhesion testing, pipette-tip probing and adhesion to a culture dish.

Results

In the shear adhesion test (Figure 1.2.4.5A), the shear force of all three hydrogels rose with displacement to a peak and then declined, with peak forces of approximately 11 N (2Y-5), 17 N (2KY-5) and 27.5 N (2KY-16). The resulting shear strengths were approximately 32, 42 and 91 kPa, respectively (no significant difference between 2Y-5 and 2KY-5; 2KY-16 significantly higher than both, p < 0.001) (Figure 1.2.4.5B). In addition, probing the hydrogel with a pipette tip (Supplementary Movie S3) and adhering it to the surface of a culture dish (Supplementary Movie S4) both demonstrated that the hydrogel has good elasticity and adhesiveness.

Figure 1.2.4.5. Shear adhesion performance of the hydrogels. (A) Shear force–displacement curves. (B) Shear strength. ns, not significant; ***, p < 0.001.

1.3 Construction and production of hydrogels with different repeat numbers

1.3.1 Plasmid construction, expression and purification of the scaffold protein 2KY-10
Recursive doubling of the scaffold

Experiment

2KY-10 was not chemically synthesized but was obtained directly from pET19b-2KY5-RDL by one round of PRe-RDL (Figure 1.3.1.1). The plasmid was divided into two aliquots: one was double-digested with AcuI + XbaI (digest A) and the other with BseRI + XbaI (digest B). All three enzymes are active at 37 °C in rCutSmart buffer and can therefore be used directly in double digestions. The digestion time was kept within 2 h and the enzyme amount did not exceed 10 U/µg to avoid the star activity of AcuI; AcuI reactions were supplemented with S-adenosylmethionine (SAM).

Digest A yielded four fragments, from which the 1008-bp target fragment containing the scaffold gene was taken (fragment F); digest B yielded two fragments, from which the 6483-bp large fragment was taken (fragment G) and the 153-bp small fragment was discarded. The two target fragments were gel-purified separately, mixed in equimolar amounts, ligated with T4 DNA ligase at 16 °C overnight, and transformed into DH5α (Figure 1.3.1.2).

The design contains a built-in safeguard worth noting. The plasmid backbone naturally carries two background AcuI sites, but these generate 3′ overhangs of CG and TT, respectively, which are not complementary to the GG overhang of the designed site; the background fragments therefore cannot be incorporated into the correct product chemically.

The 153-bp small fragment in digest B is the only possible source of religation to the parental plasmid, and it differs from the target fragment in size by more than 40-fold, so it can be completely removed by gel excision. In other words, the specificity of the entire doubling process is guaranteed by the overhang sequences and does not rely on gel resolution.

Results

Single colonies were picked for colony PCR (T7 promoter/T7 terminator primer pair), and the band shifted upward from 1152 bp for 2KY-5 to 2007 bp (Figure 1.3.1.3); the difference of 855 bp corresponds exactly to one 2KY-5 unit, demonstrating successful doubling. Sequencing confirmed that the repeat region consisted of 10 complete monomers without deletions.

The target colony was then picked for plasmid amplification. Because this is a low-copy plasmid, streptomycin was added when the culture reached an OD of approximately 0.6 to promote plasmid amplification; the plasmid was then extracted with a plasmid midi-prep kit, and the plasmid concentration and purity were measured by NanoDrop, both reaching satisfactory levels .

Production of 2KY-10

Experiment

The expression and purification of 2KY-10 followed the conditions used for 2KY-5 (induction with 1 mM IPTG for 6 h; ITC at 65 °C in PBS containing 2 M NaCl).

Results

The purification results are shown in Figure 1.3.1.4: the purification was effective, with a yield of approximately 480 mg per liter of bacterial culture, close to that of 2KY-5.

1.3.2 Plasmid construction, expression and purification of the scaffold proteins 2KY-5-Tag and 2KY-10-Tag
Insertion of SnoopTag2

Experiment

SnoopTag2 (KLGYIEFYKVEK; coding sequence of 36 bp) was introduced into pET19b-2KY5-RDL by site-directed insertion, at a position after the fifth repeat unit and before the AcuI cut site (see Table 1.1.1). This position was chosen deliberately: after insertion, the AcuI recognition site is shifted 36 bp downstream and the cut site moves accordingly, so that the RDL duplication unit changes from the 855-bp 2KY-5 to the 891-bp 2KY-5-SnoopTag2, bringing the tag into the replicable region.

This step cannot be accomplished by conventional single-fragment whole-plasmid amplification: the insertion point lies immediately adjacent to the repeat region, so that however the reverse primer is designed, its 3′ end falls within the repeat sequence and initiates extension from all five repeats simultaneously, generating a ladder of products that differ by 171 bp. At the scale of the 6.6-kb whole plasmid, these products cannot be separated, and deletion mutants would inevitably be mixed in.

We therefore adopted Method 2 of the Mut Express II kit (two-fragment amplification) and joined the two fragments by homologous recombination. An additional anchor, B, which introduces no mutation, was placed in a unique region outside the insertion point (upstream of NdeI), splitting the plasmid into two fragments that were amplified separately (Figure 1.3.2.1):

1. B→I fragment (Anchor-BF + Snp-IR): the correct product should be 956 bp.

2. I→B fragment (Snp-IF + Anchor-BR): the annealing regions of both primers are unique, yielding a single 5792-bp product.

Results

Verification of the tagged constructs

Experiment

After DpnI digestion, the two fragments were recombined using Exnase II at 37 °C for 30 min according to the ratio recommended in the manual (0.03 pmol of the longer fragment and 0.06 pmol of the shorter fragment) and transformed into DH5α.

Results

Plasmids were extracted from single colonies on the plates in the same way and subjected to colony PCR, and plasmids giving the correct band were sequenced; all sequencing results were correct. The correctly sequenced 2KY-5-Tag plasmid was transformed into E. coli BL21. In parallel, the 2KY-10-Tag plasmid was constructed by the same RDL method used for 2KY-10 and transformed into DH5α; single colonies were picked for colony PCR, and plasmids giving the correct band were sequenced, again with all results correct. Both the 2KY-5-Tag and 2KY-10-Tag plasmids were thus successfully constructed and transformed (Figure 1.3.2.2).

Production of the tagged scaffolds

Experiment

Protein expression was subsequently induced and the proteins were purified. The expression and purification of 2KY-5-Tag and 2KY-10-Tag followed the conditions used for 2KY-5 (induction with 1 mM IPTG for 6 h; ITC at 65 °C in PBS containing 2 M NaCl).

Results

The purification results are shown in Figure 1.3.2.3: the purification was effective, with yields of approximately 520 mg and 490 mg per liter of bacterial culture for 2KY-5-Tag and 2KY-10-Tag, respectively, close to that of 2KY-5.

Hydrogel scaffold — module summary

The scaffold workflow links plasmid construction, protein production and hydrogel characterization. The parental 2KY-5 construct supports recursive extension and SnoopTag2 insertion, while the expression and purification workflow is applied across the resulting scaffold series. Photocrosslinking, structural characterization and mechanical testing establish the material properties described above.

2 Safety and functional evaluation of the hydrogel

2.1 Cytotoxicity assessment

Cytotoxicity assessment

Experiment

To evaluate the cytocompatibility of the material, chondrocytes were co-cultured with hydrogel-related samples, cell viability was measured by the CCK-8 assay at 24, 48 and 72 h (Figure 2.1.1), and the viability of each group was calculated relative to the control group (Figure 2.1.2). The experimental groups comprised a dressing-solution group and low- and high-concentration G-S groups (G-S low, stock solution diluted 20-fold; G-S high, stock solution diluted 10-fold).

Results

At 24 h, the cell viability of the dressing-solution, G-S low and G-S high groups was 125.1 ± 36.3%, 110.2 ± 12.4% and 100.7 ± 12.7%, respectively; at 48 h, 134.7 ± 3.2%, 103.0 ± 4.4% and 102.7 ± 4.7%; and at 72 h, 119.0 ± 15.5%, 98.6 ± 27.6% and 88.2 ± 17.6% (percentages relative to the control group; mean ± SD, n = 3). The mean viability of every group at every time point was not lower than 88%, above the 70% threshold defined in ISO 10993-5 (a reduction of cell viability by more than 30% is considered a cytotoxic effect).([10]) Overall, these results nevertheless indicate that the material is not markedly cytotoxic.

2.2 Functional validation in chondrocytes

Chondrocyte gene-expression analysis

Experiment

To further evaluate the effect of the hydrogels on the chondrocyte phenotype, chondrocytes were co-cultured with the hydrogels (2Y-5, 2KY-5 and 2KY-16), and the expression of cartilage-related genes was measured by qPCR (Figure 2.2.1).

Results

Using the 2Y-5 group as the reference (relative expression set to 1), the expression of aggrecan (ACAN) was upregulated to approximately 78-fold and 93-fold in the 2KY-5 and 2KY-16 groups, respectively (p < 0.001), and was higher in the 2KY-16 group than in the 2KY-5 group (p < 0.05); the expression of type II collagen (COL2) was upregulated to approximately 68-fold and 85-fold, respectively (p < 0.001), and was higher in the 2KY-16 group than in the 2KY-5 group (p < 0.01); SOX9 expression was upregulated to approximately 3.2–3.3-fold (p < 0.05), with no significant difference between the two groups.

At the same time, the expression of type I collagen (COL1) decreased to approximately 0.17-fold and 0.13-fold (p < 0.001), with no significant difference between the two groups. Type X collagen (COLX) was elevated to approximately 2.7-fold in the 2KY-5 group (p < 0.05 compared with both the 2Y-5 and 2KY-16 groups), whereas there was no significant difference between the 2KY-16 and 2Y-5 groups.

These results indicate that the 2KY hydrogels promote the expression of cartilage matrix-related genes (ACAN, COL2 and SOX9) in chondrocytes and suppress COL1 expression. Increased COL1 expression is a hallmark of the loss of the cartilage phenotype (dedifferentiation) of chondrocytes in culture,([11]) and SOX9 is a key transcriptional activator of COL2 expression;([12]) this expression profile is therefore conducive to maintaining the chondrocyte phenotype. Among the groups, 2KY-16 had the stronger promoting effect on ACAN and COL2 expression.

Hydrogel evaluation — module summary

The cell experiments evaluate the hydrogel-related samples through CCK-8 measurements and cartilage-related gene expression. Together, these assays connect the material characterization to the cellular responses reported for the tested conditions.

3 Ligation system

We validated the ligation capacity and efficiency of the ligation system, which is based on the SnoopTag2–DogTag peptide–peptide ligation catalyzed by SnoopLigase2.([13–15]) We first verified the three components themselves and then extended the system to the scaffold and functional modules to verify its function in the hydrogel system.

3.1 Expression of the ligation-system proteins

Expression of the ligation-system components

Experiment

Plasmids encoding SnoopTag2-sfGFP, SUMO-DogTag and SnoopLigase2 were separately transformed into E. coli BL21(DE3) for protein expression. The expression strains were inoculated into LB liquid medium containing kanamycin (Kan) and cultured to mid-logarithmic phase, after which expression was induced with IPTG at a gradient of 0.1/0.25/0.5/1.0 mM. After culture at 16 °C for 16 h, a small volume of culture was lysed by sonication and subjected to small-scale purification by nickel-affinity chromatography. The lysates and the purified eluates were analyzed by Western blot using an anti-His primary antibody.

Results

The Western blot results confirmed that all three target proteins were successfully induced, and the optimal induction concentrations of SnoopTag2-sfGFP, SUMO-DogTag and SnoopLigase2 were 0.1 mM, 0.1 mM and 1.0 mM, respectively (Figure 3.1.1). Large-scale production was subsequently carried out under the optimal conditions determined, and expression was good for all three proteins (Figure 3.1.2).

3.2 Purification and dialysis of the ligation-system proteins

Purification and protein concentrations

Experiment

The proteins obtained from large-scale production were purified by nickel-affinity chromatography. The purified solutions of the three proteins were dialyzed in dialysis bags with a 3.5-kDa molecular weight cut-off. The dialysis buffer was PBS for SnoopTag2-sfGFP and SUMO-DogTag, and 25 mM Tris–borate (TB) buffer (pH 7.4) containing 20% (v/v) glycerol for SnoopLigase2, to preserve enzyme activity. Dialysis was carried out for 1 day with three buffer changes, and the liquid in the dialysis bags was collected after equilibration; protein concentrations were determined by the BCA assay (Figure 3.2.1).

Results

The final concentrations of the three protein solutions were: SnoopTag2-sfGFP (30 kDa), 1.33 mg/mL; SnoopLigase2 (12.9 kDa), 0.66 mg/mL; and SUMO-DogTag (14.7 kDa), 0.60 mg/mL.

3.3 Ligation reaction

Time-course analysis of ligation

Experiment

Based on the measured protein concentrations, the reaction system was prepared with all three components at a final concentration of 25 µM, and the ligation reaction was carried out at room temperature (approximately 24 °C). Samples were taken at 10, 30 and 60 min after setting up the reaction, and the reactions were terminated by boiling. The individual components and the samples from the different reaction times were analyzed by SDS-PAGE.

Results

The results showed that ligation had occurred within 10 min (a distinct ligation-product band of approximately 45 kDa appeared, consistent with the sum of SUMO-DogTag at 14.7 kDa and SnoopTag2-sfGFP at 30 kDa) and was complete within 1 h (the band of SUMO-DogTag, which was present in lower amount, disappeared), demonstrating that the ligation reaction is very rapid and efficient (Figure 3.3.1).

Ligation system — module summary

The ligation workflow covers production and purification of the three components, followed by a time-course assay of the reaction. The results connect preparation of the ligation-system proteins with the formation of the ligation product shown in the original gel.

Platform summary

The scaffold-group work brings together a programmable protein scaffold, a hydrogel preparation workflow, material and cellular characterization, and a peptide ligation system. These experimental stages provide the basis for assembling and evaluating the platform described in this section.
